clue.text: Zombie family member's backing off, clutching something red

indicators.note: to clutch is to grip tightly, so one piece wraps its arms around the other
the back of a word is its final letter, and taking that off trims the word at its end

parts.note: an aunt is a relative
a ripe tomato is red

explanation.surface: A horror tale: some zombie relative retreats, gripping something bloody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing off' reads as retreating, but it means the back letter comes off. 'Something red' is a vegetable, not blood.
explanation.definitionFit: A zombie is a person acting mechanically without thought, just like a robot or mindless machine.

clue.text: One opposed to having colonist on top of column

parts.note: ants live in colonies
the letter I looks like an upright column

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a settler being placed atop a pillar.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on top of' puts the first piece above the second. 'Colonist' suggests a settler, but it is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a noun, the word means a person who is against something, an opponent.

clue.text: Archaic word for U K

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the old second-person pronoun, U being text-speak for 'you'
second meaning: informal word for a thousand, which K abbreviates

explanation.walkthrough: The spaced 'U K' looks like the United Kingdom; split it into U (you) and K (a thousand).
explanation.definitionFit: Old English addressed one person as thou, and slang shortens a thousand pounds to a thou, written K.

clue.text: Large study of participation in church services?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the famous British social research project begun in 1937, recording everyday life on a huge scale

definitions.note: a whimsical reading of the phrase as watching Mass
definitions.meaning: second meaning, playful: attending Mass, the Catholic service, is observing it

explanation.walkthrough: Mass Observation was a British project that collected diaries and reports from ordinary people. Mass is the Catholic church service, and to observe a rite is to keep it.
explanation.definitionFit: The project was a large-scale sociological survey, and the question mark flags the punning religious reading.

clue.text: Bones of sailors on bottom of Mississippi

parts.note: tar is old slang for a sailor

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom of a word is its final letter

parts.note: final letter of the river's name

explanation.surface: Sailors' skeletons lie on the bed of the Mississippi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' in a down clue places the sailors above the letter taken from the river.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarsi are the small bones of the ankle and upper foot, plural of tarsus.

clue.text: No herons _____ to be seen? Never mind

parts.note: surface padding: opens the list of absent birds that the gap continues
the gap continues the list of absences with 'nor ...'
egrets are a kind of heron, the second missing bird that fills the gap
surface padding completing the birdwatcher's sentence

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher laments a heronless marsh, then shrugs it off.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill the blank with a phrase about more missing birds; re-spaced, the same letters make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying you have no regrets is an idiom for dismissing a disappointment, like shrugging and saying forget it.

clue.text: Fed up with education after exam

parts.note: the SAT is an American college admission test
common abbreviation for education

explanation.surface: A student is sick of school after sitting an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed up' looks like boredom but is meant literally: filled with food.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stuffed full of food is to be satisfied completely, having eaten enough.

clue.text: Being flexible with worker lacking aspiration, cut workforce down — that'll regulate prices

indicators.note: aspiration is the breathy h-sound, so lacking it drops that letter

parts.note: an adverb form of supple, in a flexible manner
a hand is a labourer, as in farmhand
to deman is to reduce the staff of a business
standard abbreviation for down

explanation.surface: Management talk of flexibility and job cuts dressed up as price control.
explanation.walkthrough: HAND loses its H to give AND; DEMAN (reduce staff) plus D for down completes the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: The economic law balancing what sellers offer against what buyers want sets the market cost of goods.

clue.text: Set of novelties I flogged

indicators.note: something flogged is beaten about, knocking these letters out of order

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A trader sold off a collection of novelty items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flogged' reads as sold, but it is the anagram signal; 'Set' starts the clue and is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A TV set is the household receiving device, so the short noun stands for the whole appliance.

clue.text: Bandage ear, say, knowing what to put on

parts.note: to dress a wound is to bandage it
hearing is one of the five senses; 'say' marks the ear as an example

explanation.surface: First aid instructions: bind up the ear, and know which dressing to apply.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests knowing which bandage to apply; really it is about clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Good taste in choosing clothes is the ability to select the right outfit to wear.

clue.text: Appropriate to wake between 3 and 5 in afternoon

indicators.note: a piece set between two others is surrounded by them
the numbers pick out the third and fifth letters of the following word

parts.note: letters three and five of the word
to rouse someone is to wake them

explanation.surface: Siesta advice: the right time to wake is between three and five pm.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 3 and 5 as clock times; they are letter positions. 'Appropriate' is the verb, to take.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouser money is British slang for pocketing it, often improperly, so it means to seize for oneself.

clue.text: Put off touching vegan food

parts.note: re means about or concerning
pulses such as lentils and beans are plant protein

explanation.surface: Someone is turned off by the idea of eating vegan fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touching' means concerning, a common crossword route to RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To disgust or drive back someone is to repel them, which is what the phrasal verb means here.

clue.text: Packing items of PPE, they'll help deliver jabs

parts.note: to box things is to pack them
gloves are personal protective equipment

explanation.surface: A vaccination centre stocks up on protective kit for the people giving injections.
explanation.walkthrough: PPE and jabs conjure a vaccine clinic; the jabs are punches.
explanation.definitionFit: A jab is a quick straight punch in the ring, thrown wearing padded fistwear.

clue.text: A copper's arranged to take place as star investigator?

indicators.note: arranging things puts them into a new order

parts.note: the letters taken as written
to be can mean to happen or occur

explanation.surface: A police officer is set up to become a celebrated detective.
explanation.walkthrough: The copper and investigator suggest police work, but the investigator explores the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: An unmanned craft sent to gather data in the cosmos investigates stars and planets, hence the playful question mark.

clue.text: Sex coming up in wedding photos perhaps results in fighting between partners?

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: marital means relating to marriage
photography is an example of art
it is a coy word for sex; those two letters already sit inside the wedding word, and they are what gets turned over

explanation.surface: Racy wedding pictures lead to a row between husband and wife.
explanation.walkthrough: The sex word is already sitting inside the wedding word; only those two letters flip, which is what turns married into fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Judo and karate are practised with a sparring opponent, so combat sports pit training partners against each other.

clue.text: Smooth operator taking one in — I'll find belief in odd places

indicators.note: to take something in is to absorb it inside oneself

parts.note: the plus sign is a mathematical operator
a means one
taken as written

indicators.note: the first, third and fifth positions are the odd-numbered spots

parts.note: letters one, three and five of the word

explanation.surface: A con man reels someone in, and the mark finds faith in strange places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smooth operator' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just 'Smooth'; the operator is a maths sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A plausible person is glib and persuasive, seeming honest on the surface, as a slick talker does.

clue.text: Inspired Messiah? Not him, sick inside and tense

indicators.note: something inside sits within the enclosing piece

parts.note: from Monty Python's Life of Brian: 'He's not the Messiah'
ill means sick
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A doubter rejects an inspired messiah, feeling queasy and nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: In the film Life of Brian, his mother insists 'He's not the Messiah, he's a very naughty boy'; ILL goes inside that name, then T.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspired work shows outstanding talent or genius, so the two adjectives are close synonyms.

clue.text: Part of supermarket beer is stocked

indicators.note: what is stocked is held within the store, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
taken as written

explanation.surface: Directions to the shelf where the beer is kept.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'is' does double duty in the surface but is just its own letters inside the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoppers walk along the passages between shelves, each a section of the shop.

clue.text: Sharper knife's lost one time

indicators.note: something lost is gone, so a letter drops away

parts.note: a cutter is a blade or knife
T is the abbreviation for time; only one of its two copies goes

explanation.surface: A knife that was once keen has lost its edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sharper' suggests a blade, but it means quicker-witted.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute can mean clever or shrewd, especially in British and American informal use, so cuter is the comparative of clever.

clue.text: Short position with private knowledge, obtaining debt pledges — sneaky!

indicators.note: something cut short has lost its final letter

parts.note: someone on the inside has privileged information
an IOU is a written promise to repay

explanation.surface: Financial jargon about short-selling on insider information and taking on debt: a shady deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short position' is a trading term, but 'Short' is the cue to clip the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something insidious works in a stealthy, harmful way, creeping in unnoticed like a sly scheme.

clue.text: Take on role of a Birmingham criminal, perhaps, and perform brilliantly

definitions.text: Take on role of a Birmingham criminal, perhaps
definitions.meaning: first meaning: act a member of the Peaky Blinders, a real Birmingham gang dramatised on TV
second meaning: British idiom for an outstanding performance, especially in sport

explanation.walkthrough: The Peaky Blinders were a Birmingham street gang around 1900, famous now from the BBC drama; a blinder is British slang for a superb display.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a player who has an excellent game is said to have had a dazzling match, a blinding one.

clue.text: Specialised market in organic hemp

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the following words, running across the gap

parts.note: spans the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A small sector of trade dealing in organically grown hemp.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the gap between the two words, using the end of the first and the start of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche market is a narrow segment of buyers with particular tastes, served by specialist sellers.

clue.text: Press cull removing head

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is taken away

parts.note: to purge is to get rid of, eliminate

explanation.surface: Newspapers are culled with the editor beheaded: a grim media purge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like journalism but is the verb, to push someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To press someone to act is to urge them, push or encourage strongly.

clue.text: Nose endlessly runs with it

definitions.note: the whole clue doubles as the definition

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is dropped
running colours or letters spread out of place and mix

parts.note: the word with its last letter removed
it shortened to 't, as in ''twas'

explanation.surface: A cold that will not end: the nose keeps running.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also reads as a definition: what a streaming nose runs with. 'T is the old clipped form of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mucus is the slimy discharge from a runny nose, and the blunt slang word for it fits here.

clue.text: Old empress abandoning zither's beginning another instrument

parts.note: standard abbreviation for old

indicators.note: to abandon something is to leave it behind, so a letter goes

parts.note: a czarina was a Russian empress

indicators.note: a word's beginning is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of the stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A former empress gives up the zither and takes up a different instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' is not part of the empress; it is O, standing in front. 'Another' refers back to the zither in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument, a further example of a musical instrument.

clue.text: Tea will put a smile on feelings of vexation

definitions.note: the answer is a single uncountable noun; the clue phrases it as plural

parts.note: cha (or char) is British slang for tea
a grin is a broad smile

explanation.surface: A cuppa cheers you up when you are annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: Cha is old British slang for tea, from the Chinese word.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is annoyance or distress at having failed or been humiliated, a sense of mortified irritation.

clue.text: Fed's letter intercepted by another

indicators.note: something intercepted is caught midway along its path, so one piece ends up inside the other

parts.note: en is the spelt-out name of the letter N
another word for 'fed', the clue's definition

explanation.surface: An FBI agent's mail is seized by someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' looks like another letter, but it means another word for the definition. Fed, an American FBI agent, is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are past participles of verbs about consuming food: having been given a meal versus having consumed it.

clue.text: Falls in river with utmost style

indicators.note: one piece placed within another

parts.note: the Trent is a major river of the English Midlands
to fall in battle is to die

explanation.surface: Someone plunges into a river, but does it with great panache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falls' suggests a waterfall beside the river; here it is the verb, to perish, as soldiers fall.
explanation.definitionFit: The most fashionable or up-to-date thing has the greatest style, so the superlative adjective matches.
